groups.title: Questions 11-16
groups.instruction: What is each of the following sites famous for?

options.text: factories making food with natural ingredients

transcript.text: Part 2. You will hear a woman introducing different sites to a group of tourists.
First you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.
Good morning tourists, I am Jane and welcome to Hampshire. I am very happy to see you all here and I can promise you a very nice time here.
We would be visiting six different places which are renowned for different activities of their own.
We would begin from Jackson Town, which is known for its buggy ride.
Rather than sit in a train, you will sit in a small, lightweight carriage pulled by a single horse.
It was named after Sanya Jackson who was famous for her generosity in the region.
The locals even built a museum for her.
Belleville would be our next stop. We'll get there by helicopter.
Oh, I almost forgot that this mode of transportation has been suspended because of the variable weather.
We will get there by taking a jolly train ride, which is a highlight in this area.
The people here are very friendly and would always try to make you feel as comfortable as possible.
They entertain their guests with local delicacies like cakes and pastries which are quite famous in this area.
Albany is a very lively and playful place, so get ready for some good and hearty laughs.
It is usually fun to watch some people screaming during a balloon trip which is quite popular there.
Albany also features cool relaxation spots where you can just take time to cool off and enjoy yourself.
Fort Scott is where we have Jackson's biscuits, which is famous for its teddy bear shapes.
There you can get to see how they're pieced together.
The location also has a small refreshment section where you can grab a bite.
The chiffon cakes there are just palatable.
Rawlings has many factories there.
Among these factories, the ones that make cakes are gaining more fame than others.
Their cakes are made from pure cream, cheese, eggs and sugar, no food additive.
I always advise our tourists to get some for themselves and their families as their products will never disappoint you.
Rawlings Council has decided to combine their products with the native culture in the future, which will be a strong selling point.
Greensville boasts about its native American culture which is widely known.
A lot of artifacts have been collected around here and now kept in the local art museum for studies and tourists, sake.
A lot of people who had been looking for their roots have been able to make a sort of connection by coming to this place.
The museum has been around for decades and it was recently renovated.
However, the story has not changed.
Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.
Now let me briefly talk about other buildings and sites in Greensville.
Please take a look at the map which I gave you earlier.
Greensville has a good kindergarten for younger children and it is situated just to the north of Monument Street.
It has well-trained teachers and a conducive environment for learning.
As it's receiving an increasing number of children, the City Council has decided to move it to a larger site on Oak Road this November.
The new spot is uncertain though.
We also have a craft shop which is at the end of Ash Road.
The craft shop is for displaying all types of art and drawings, paintings and the likes.
It is a key feature of Greensville due to its art exhibitions which run three times a year.
Wixson's school used to be situated at the intersection of Oak Road and George Avenue.
But the site wasn't big enough as the number of students kept growing.
So the larger piece of land right beside the old location has become the new site for the school since last year.
It is important to note that the school has been around for a while.
There are well-experienced teachers to help students develop at their own pace.
The cake factory that we spoke about is actually between Monument Street and Maple Street just by the roadside.
The people of Greensville are very hospitable.
